children: shares fell 3.5% in extended trading on Thursday after the Photoshop maker reported second-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's estimates.

For the period ending Aug. 28, Adobe said it earned an adjusted $6.13 per share as revenue rose 13% year-over-year to $6.76B. Subscription revenue accounted for $6.58B during the period, while product revenue was $67M.
Analysts had expected the company to earn $6.08 per share on $6.7B in revenue.
Total annualized recurring revenue exiting the quarter was $27.5B, Adobe added.
“Adobe delivered record Q3 results, reflecting the strength of our AI innovation, expanding customer reach and leadership across creativity, productivity and customer experience,”

Shantanu Narayen, chair and CEO, Adobe. “Reaching a landmark of more than one billion monthly active users is a defining moment for Adobe, and I have confidence that Anil will build on this momentum to drive Adobe's next chapter of growth and innovation in the AI era.”

Looking to the fiscal fourth quarter, Adobe said it expects adjusted earnings between $6.30 and $6.35 per share, above the $6.30 per share estimate. Revenue is forecast to be between $6.8B and $6.85B, with the midpoint of $6.825B slightly below the $6.84B analysts were expecting.

For the full year, Adobe now expects to earn between $24.45 and $24.50 per share on an adjusted basis, up from a previous range of $24.35 to $24.45 per share, with the midpoint above the $24.40 per share estimate. Revenue is now forecast to be between $26.58B and $26.63B, above the prior forecast of $26.5B to $26.6B, with the midpoint well above the $26.56B estimate.
The company will host a conference call at 5 p.m. EST to discuss the results.

title: Adobe slips even as it boosts full-year earnings outlook after strong Q2 results
